corpus.filter: non-home planets with non-null winner label
corpus.label: captured by eventual winner within first 100 turns

features: visibility (frac of others reachable without sun block)
orbital_reach_seat0 (frac of orbital period closer to seat-0 home)
model: logistic regression (sklearn LogisticRegression, C=1.0), 5-fold stratified CV, StandardScaler

falsification_gate.description: Mean 5-fold AUC >= 0.70 indicates geometric features genuinely predict capture priority.

headline_findings: AUC 0.77 confirms geometric features carry real signal for capture priority.
Two features dominate (>0.7 absolute coefficient): planet RADIUS (production proxy via radius = 1 + ln(prod)) and STARTING SHIPS (lower garrison -> more likely captured).
production's raw coefficient (-0.07) is misleading — it is fully absorbed by `radius`, which is collinear and scaled. The real production signal is +0.78 via radius.

min_home_dist (+0.21) is positive: top-10 winners reach FAR planets by step 100, not just close ones. The closer planets are taken in the opening (Mine 3); the longer-arm captures are what separate winners from losers.

orbital_reach (+0.40, but raw means tied at 0.498) — sklearn picks up an interaction; raw univariate inspection shows the marginal is noise. Coefficient may be a high-variance fit; do NOT use this term standalone.

DENIAL_SCORE (rahul-style neutral-denial near enemy) is effectively ZERO (-0.035). Either our formulation is wrong or this is not a winner-distinguishing feature in the top-10 corpus. Reformulate or drop.
downstream_uses: Feeds Experiment Option 2 (planet-value head replacement) — use the standardised coefficients above as initial weights.
Production-weighting via radius (not production directly) is the cleanest single signal.
Garrison-aware target selection deserves a dedicated 'easy-pickings' bonus already in ROI; this validates the coefficient sign.
